newsitem.title: ITALY: Bomb goes off at Milan city hall, no injuries.
newsitem.headline: Bomb goes off at Milan city hall, no injuries.

text.p: A bomb exploded outside Milan's city hall on Friday, causing damage but no injuries, in an attack carried out just three days before elections for the post of mayor in Italy's business capital.
The blast also coincided with the anniversary of Italy's World War Two liberation in 1945. It damaged the back wall of the city hall and shattered windows in several buildings.
Police said the device, made of gunpowder and iron bolts packed into a steel container, had exploded at around 4.30 a.m. There was no immediate claim of responsibility.

Politicians from across the spectrum, including Milan's outgoing mayor Marco Formentini of the separatist Northern League, linked the explosion to Sunday's elections and to the April 25 anniversary, a national holiday.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi was expected to visit the scene later in the day, government sources said.
"The choice of day and where the bomb was placed are evidently significant," deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni told reporters.

"It is an attempt to mark a date which is a festival of democracy...Naturally, putting the bomb at city hall also has another meaning, at a time when the city is engaged in an election campaign," he said.
The race for Milan's mayor is the most significant in elections on Sunday for local councils and mayors in more than 1,000 towns and cities across Italy.

Formentini, elected in 1993, faces possible defeat in Sunday's first round to rivals from Prodi's centre-left Olive Tree alliance and the main opposition centre-right bloc. A run-off is scheduled for May 11.
Italy's World War Two liberation from Nazi German occupation and the remnants of Italian Fascist rule was completed on April 25, 1945 after a bitter partisan struggle.
Dictator Benito Mussolini was subsequently captured and shot by partisans and his body brought to Milan and strung up in public.
